answer.label: Not Maya Angelou — a line from ‘Touched by an Angel’
answer.authorName: Touched by an Angel (the character Tess)
answer.authorDates: CBS drama, 1994–2003 · line spoken by Tess (Della Reese) in 1995
answer.sourceLine: The exact wording appears in none of Maya Angelou’s books, poems, essays, or recorded interviews. Wikiquote files it under Misattributed, and the earliest documented, near-identical line is dialogue written for the angel Tess in the 1995 CBS series Touched by an Angel: “hate has caused a lot of problems in this world, but it’s never solved one yet.” The polished “Maya Angelou” form is a later, slightly reworded internet variant.

source.excerpt: No, hate has caused a lot of problems in this world, but it’s never solved one yet.
trail: Wikiquote lists this line in its Misattributed section for Maya Angelou, flagging a nearly identical line from the 1995 series Touched by an Angel.
That line is spoken by the angel Tess in the episode “The Big Bang” (season 2, aired 25 Nov 1995): “hate has caused a lot of problems in this world, but it’s never solved one yet.”
The smoothed, Angelou-credited wording now circulates on aggregators such as Goodreads, yet appears in none of her books, poems, or interviews.
source.excerptNote: The earliest documented form of the line, spoken by Tess to a bank robber. The version pinned on Maya Angelou drops “this,” swaps “it’s never” for “has not,” and adds her name — but matches nothing in her own writing.
source.rightsHolder: CBS and the producers of Touched by an Angel
source.rightsNote: The exact phrasing is not from Maya Angelou; its earliest documented form is a line of scripted dialogue in the 1995 CBS series Touched by an Angel, a work still under copyright. No public-domain source exists for this wording.

author.name: Maya Angelou
author.heading: About Maya Angelou
author.bio: Maya Angelou (1928–2014) was an American poet, memoirist, and civil-rights activist, celebrated for I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings and for reciting “On the Pulse of Morning” at Bill Clinton’s 1993 inauguration. Her stature as a moral voice makes her one of the internet’s most frequent magnets for uplifting lines she never wrote — this hate aphorism among them.

misattribution.heading: How Angelou got the credit
misattribution.intro: This is a textbook celebrity-magnet misattribution: a memorable line of television dialogue re-credited to a beloved author who never said it.

items.why: The wording appears in none of Angelou’s books, poems, essays, or interviews. Wikiquote lists it in its Misattributed section and points to the 1995 TV script as the near-identical source.

misattribution.truthLine: The earliest documented version is dialogue for the angel Tess in the Touched by an Angel episode “The Big Bang” (1995) — not anything Maya Angelou is known to have written or said.

context.heading: Why it matters
lead: The sentiment — that hatred creates problems but never fixes them — is an old moral commonplace. What is specific here is the phrasing, and that phrasing was written for television. In the second-season Touched by an Angel episode “The Big Bang” (aired 25 November 1995), Della Reese’s character Tess tells a bank robber, “hate has caused a lot of problems in this world, but it’s never solved one yet.”

Somewhere in the years of copy-paste the line lost its “this,” traded “it’s never” for “has not,” picked up Maya Angelou’s name, and hardened into a quote-card staple. It now circulates on Goodreads and countless image macros — but appears in none of Angelou’s own work.
context.pull: “Hate has caused a lot of problems in this world, but it’s never solved one yet” — not Angelou, but the angel Tess.
